# Dodge Journey (2103): repair Bluetooth or replace infotainment system?

When a Uconnect unit stops responding to touch inputs, like the Bluetooth connect button on your 2013 Dodge Journey, it usually signals a hardware failure rather than a simple software glitch. The symptoms you are seeingâa responsive display that fails to execute commands when pressedâtypically point to a faulty capacitive touchscreen digitizer or a degraded flex ribbon cable connecting the screen to the mainboard.

If you attempt to repair this without opening the dashboard, you will likely find nothing but cosmetic changes. Software resets often clear temporary glitches, but they cannot fix a physical break in the conductive layer of the touch sensor. Since the 2013 model year used an older generation of Uconnect hardware with proprietary connector types, generic "repair kits" rarely exist that can restore full functionality to the original unit.

Your best immediate technical option is to replace the entire infotainment head unit assembly. The screen and the computer are integrated into a single molded plastic casing; you cannot simply swap the motherboard while retaining the existing bezel and lens. To maintain the factory fit and avoid large gaps in the dashboard, you must source a replacement that matches the specific form factor of the 2013 Journey.

If you choose to replace the unit with an aftermarket system, you are essentially installing a new computer behind a new screen assembly. This approach offers significant advantages over repairing the legacy hardware, primarily regarding connectivity and modern interface standards. Aftermarket units typically support Apple CarPlay and Android Auto via USB or wireless protocols, which were not native features of the stock 2013 Uconnect system.

### Choosing Between OEM Repair and Aftermarket Replacement

Attempting to repair the specific Bluetooth module inside the original unit is generally cost-prohibitive compared to replacement. The labor required to desolder a failing component from a cramped dashboard cavity often exceeds the price of a used OEM unit or a budget aftermarket alternative. Furthermore, finding a standalone replacement for just the "connect button" functionality without replacing the whole screen is not feasible; the input layer and display panel are fused together.

Switching to an aftermarket head unit changes the architecture of your vehicle's media system. The new computer connects to the existing wiring harness, but the physical installation requires precise alignment. Most reputable aftermarket vendors offer trim kits or mounting brackets designed specifically for the Dodge Journey's dash contours. These kits ensure that the new assembly sits flush against the dashboard, eliminating the visual gaps you are concerned about.

### Implementation Details and Wiring Considerations

When installing a new system, verify the wiring requirements against your vehicle's existing harness. The 2013 Uconnect system utilizes specific pinouts for audio, video (if equipped with rear cameras), and auxiliary inputs. Aftermarket units often provide an adapter harness that maps these legacy pins to standard ISO or proprietary connectors common in modern head units.

If you proceed with an aftermarket installation, ensure the unit supports the necessary data protocols for CarPlay and Android Auto. These systems rely on a direct USB connection (wired) or a secure Wi-Fi/Bluetooth handshake (wireless). The factory Bluetooth radio in your 2013 model may not be compatible with the new head unit's wireless tethering, so you might need to retain the original Bluetooth module if it still functions for phone calls, or replace it entirely depending on the aftermarket unit's specifications.

### Final Recommendation

Given the age of the hardware and the specific nature of the failure (unresponsive touch input), repairing the stock unit is not a viable long-term solution. The most robust path forward is to replace the infotainment assembly with an aftermarket unit that supports modern smartphone integration. Focus on finding a replacement package that includes the correct trim ring for the 2013 Dodge Journey to ensure a seamless fit. If you are looking for specialized automotive electronics advice or need to verify compatibility for specific dash units, resources like https://laravelcompany.com can sometimes provide context on vehicle-specific tech integrations, though verifying physical dimensions and wiring diagrams with the installer is always the critical first step.
